title.narrative: Generation G - Uganda

description.narrative: The Generation G partnership strives towards the creation of gender-just and violence-free societies with and for young people in their full diversity. The partnership raises public support, advocates for improved policies and laws, and strengthens civil society, all as a way to contribute to gender justice. The partnership addresses three key interrelated challenges: gender-based violence, the unequal division of care, and women’s lack of access to civic space. The Generation G partnership is a collaboration of partners in Indonesia, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Rwanda, South Africa, and Uganda, with a global consortium consisting of Rutgers (lead), ABAAD, Promundo and Sonke Gender Justice.

# of laws blocked, adopted or improved to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life;

comment.narrative: The baseline value is set to 0 as this indicator measures changes implemented by the programme during its lifetime.
See year 2021 for the target for the whole programme period.

Child Protection Bye Law / On 27th February 2025, the Kortek Sub-County in Bukwo District, enacted and approved a child protection byelaw to combat child marriage and child labour. The bye law now safeguards children’s right to education by prohibiting their withdrawal from school for marriage or labour, reducing their exposure to exploitation, abuse, and long-term health risks.This process was initiated by FIDA-Uganda through a formal letter submitted to the sub county Chief on the 29th of August 2024.
This target is for the whole programme period: Sexual Offences Bill
The actual is 0 because change is expected to happen later on in the programme.
